authored_from: Articles (Serious)/technical/3B1B — Monitor - Formal Execution.md, §V (EWMA — smooth telemetry without lag) and §VI (Anomaly detection — when to stop watching and start looking)
note: SPEC vectors for the detector layer over the W = d(s,V) series: EWMA smoothing, CUSUM for persistent shifts, and the severity classification that IS the Monitor→Controller boundary. Authored from the article, not generated from the reference engine.

divergence.statement: The reference engine has no time series at all, so it has nothing for a detector to run over.

term_by_term.a W series to detect over: RUST-AHEAD, and prerequisite. The reference's urgency is `pct = spent/allocated` computed fresh per render — a single scalar, not a series. There is no history of the quantity, so there is nothing to smooth or accumulate. This module could not exist there until region.rs's d(s,V) did.
term_by_term.EWMA (§V): RUST-AHEAD. Grep-0. Raw values go straight to the surface, which is the jitter §V opens by describing — 'a budget ring that flickers every second trains the eye to ignore it'.
term_by_term.CUSUM (§VI): RUST-AHEAD. Grep-0. The reference has no notion of a PERSISTENT shift: every reading is judged alone, so 5% over for ten consecutive days and one 50% spike that corrects are indistinguishable to it.
term_by_term.the Monitor→Controller boundary: RUST-AHEAD. §VI calls the CUSUM detector 'the formal boundary between watching and looking'. In the reference there is no boundary because there is no detector — surfacing is decided by the Curated UI's knapsack on a per-render urgency score, with no concept of escalation.

divergence.what_python_does_have_and_why_it_is_not_: The reference DOES have a real attention budget: curated_ui.py's knapsack picks ~4 widgets by salience, and that genuinely limits what a person is shown. But budgeting WHAT to show is not the same as deciding WHETHER anything has changed enough to warrant showing — a knapsack always fills its slots. CUSUM answers a question the knapsack never asks.
divergence.an_article_defect_levelled_up_not_copied: §VI's pseudocode zeroes S_pos BEFORE calling classify(), which reads max(S_pos, S_neg)/h — so an upward shift would report excess ≈ 0 and classify INFO, never escalating however extreme. The prose is unambiguous (> 3.0 → CRITICAL), so the ordering is the error, not the rule. Implemented as the prose specifies: the excess is captured at the moment of the alert, then the accumulator resets. Recorded here rather than silently 'fixed'.
divergence.when_python_catches_up: These cases become parity vectors unchanged; nothing in them is Rust-specific.
divergence.not_a_divergence_in: R1 behaviour. The detectors are a new additive module and touch no existing gate path.

ewma_cases.name: the_first_observation_seeds_the_level
ewma_cases.why: Starting from zero would make every series appear to ramp up from nothing — a fabricated transient in the one signal everything else trusts.

ewma_cases.name: smoothing_converges_on_a_new_level_rather_than_jumping_to_it
ewma_cases.why: §V's whole purpose: smooth signal that stays responsive. Raw telemetry jitters, and a widget that flickers trains the eye to ignore it.

ewma_cases.name: a_smaller_alpha_smooths_harder
ewma_cases.why: The declared tradeoff. A budget ring can be cosmetically smooth; a constraint-health indicator must respond within seconds. Same series, two declared α, two different answers.

ewma_cases.name: the_half_life_says_what_the_chosen_alpha_actually_buys
ewma_cases.why: 'α = 0.1' says little to whoever has to argue about it; 'half-life ≈ 7 updates' says what it costs. These are the article's own worked values.

ewma_cases.name: alpha_is_bounded_at_both_ends
ewma_cases.why: α = 1 is no smoothing (use the raw series) and α = 0 never moves at all. Both endpoints are excluded deliberately.

cusum_cases.name: a_small_persistent_drift_alerts
cusum_cases.why: THE property CUSUM exists for, and the reason it is not a threshold. W sitting at 2 against an expected 0 adds (2 − 0 − 1) = 1 per step, so S⁺ crosses h = 10 on the eleventh.

cusum_cases.name: a_single_much_larger_spike_that_corrects_does_not
cusum_cases.why: THE PROOF OF VALUE, and the article's own comparison: a budget 5% over for ten consecutive days is more alarming than a single 50% spike that immediately corrects. Here the spike is 4.5× the drift value of the case above and still never fires, because it does not persist — it decays back to zero on its own.

cusum_cases.name: the_accumulator_resets_when_the_process_returns_to_normal
cusum_cases.why: Evidence for a shift that stopped is not kept forever. The cumulative sum grows on a persistent shift and resets on return to normal — both halves matter.

cusum_cases.name: a_downward_shift_is_detected_too
cusum_cases.why: S⁻ is not decoration. On a W series a sustained DROP is the household recovering — moving back toward the viable region — and that is worth knowing as much as drifting away.

cusum_cases.name: delta_sets_the_smallest_shift_worth_noticing
cusum_cases.why: A drift inside the δ band never accumulates at all. That is the declared parameter doing its job, not the detector missing something — δ IS 'the minimum shift you care about detecting'.

cusum_cases.name: the_declared_threshold_changes_when_a_person_is_interrupted
cusum_cases.why: h is 'how much evidence do you want before being interrupted' — a judgement about THIS household, which is exactly why it is a spec field and not a constant. Same series, two declared patiences, two different answers.

severity_cases.name: the_severity_table_is_the_articles
severity_cases.why: excess = max(S⁺,S⁻)/h, with strict inequalities exactly as §VI writes them.

severity_cases.name: warning_and_critical_cross_the_boundary_and_info_does_not
severity_cases.why: §VI: 'the CUSUM detector is the formal boundary between watching and looking.' CRITICAL and WARNING escalate to the Controller; INFO stays in the Monitor. This is the seam CTL-7 will consume.

severity_cases.name: a_severe_shift_escalates_rather_than_reporting_info
severity_cases.why: THE ARTICLE'S PSEUDOCODE DEFECT, pinned. It zeroes S_pos before calling classify(), which reads max(S_pos,S_neg)/h — so an upward shift would always report excess ≈ 0 and classify INFO, never escalating however extreme. The prose is unambiguous, so the ordering is the error. The excess is captured at the moment of the alert, then the accumulator resets.

declaration_cases.name: a_zero_threshold_is_rejected
declaration_cases.why: h = 0 alerts on everything, which is the same as no detector at all — and silence-by-noise is worse than silence.

declaration_cases.name: a_negative_delta_is_rejected
declaration_cases.why: A negative minimum-shift-worth-detecting inverts the accumulator.

pipeline_cases.name: a_household_sitting_inside_v_never_escalates
pipeline_cases.why: W = 0 throughout. Nothing to look at, and watching stays cheap — which is the point of separating the two.

pipeline_cases.name: a_household_drifting_out_of_v_eventually_gets_looked_at
pipeline_cases.why: The end-to-end shape: a sustained distance from the viable region crosses the boundary. NOT on the first sample — that would be a threshold, not a CUSUM.

pipeline_cases.name: the_pipeline_smooths_before_it_detects
pipeline_cases.why: CUSUM sees the EWMA level, not the raw series. Feeding it raw would let a single jittery sample push the accumulator — exactly the spike sensitivity CUSUM exists to avoid. The two detectors are a pipeline, not alternatives. The raw W is still carried alongside, because that is what a person is told.
